body:
• New Zealand white-ball captain Mitchell Santner, 34, turned down a lucrative two-year offer from the Adelaide Strikers in Australia's Big Bash League to remain on a New Zealand central contract.
  • Accepting the deal would have required him to give up his central contract — and likely the captaincy: "I don't want to give up captaincy... it was a no-brainer for me," he told the New Zealand Herald.
  • The decision keeps him available for New Zealand's marquee summer: a home series against India (October 22 – December 1, 2026) followed by a four-Test tour of Australia.
  • His choice contrasts with teammates including Mark Chapman, who moved to a casual contract to chase BBL money — a trend Santner says NZ Cricket can't match financially: "We aren't going to keep up with the money."

Mitchell Santner has chosen the black cap over the big cheque. New Zealand's white-ball captain turned down what he described as a genuinely tempting two-year offer from the Adelaide Strikers in Australia's Big Bash League, deciding instead to keep his New Zealand central contract — and the captaincy that comes with it.

The offer was first reported by News Corp, with ESPNcricinfo reporting it was a two-year deal that would have required Santner to surrender his central contract. "The offer was good, I'm not going to lie," he told the New Zealand Herald. "I did entertain the thought of it, but... even if I'm not going to play every game of test cricket I still feel like there's a role for me."

The captaincy was the decider

For Santner, the arithmetic was about more than money. "If that was part of the deal, it was a no-brainer for me," he said of keeping the captaincy. "Sitting without a central contract and trying to captain, I don't know if that would sit right."

"When you look ahead to the summer we've got, India here for white ball and Tests and Australia away – there's not many bigger than that – it's a pretty exciting time. I'd like to still be part of that."

— Mitchell Santner

A summer built around India

The schedule Santner is protecting is one of the most demanding in recent New Zealand memory: a home white-ball and Test series against India from October 22 to December 1, 2026, followed by a four-Test tour of Australia. Beyond that lie an ODI World Cup and, in 2028, a T20 World Cup hosted in New Zealand. "We've got a World Cup next year, a T20 World Cup in New Zealand the year after," he said.

Background: the casual-contract exodus

Santner's loyalty stands in deliberate contrast to a growing trend among his teammates. Mark Chapman (32, 129 white-ball caps) dropped his central contract for a casual deal to chase a BBL opportunity — a move that opened a first full contract for fast bowler Matt Fisher. Devon Conway, Lockie Ferguson, Finn Allen, Adam Milne and Tim Seifert have all taken casual NZC contracts to play franchise leagues while staying available for selection.

Santner was candid about the economics driving those choices: "We aren't going to keep up with the money for some of these other opportunities... If it is a casual contract, that's the way to keep guys invested and playing for New Zealand." The Adelaide Strikers, notably, have also signed Ben Stokes, while Finn Allen was poached by the Melbourne Stars in a big BBL deal.

What's next

Santner will now lead New Zealand into the India series — the marquee home assignment of the summer — with his central contract and captaincy intact. His decision is a rare win for national boards in the ongoing tug-of-war with franchise leagues, and it sets up a fascinating captaincy subplot when he faces the Indian side that so many of his former teammates have chased abroad.
diaspora_angle: The India vs New Zealand home series is the marquee event Santner prioritised — directly relevant to the Indian cricket diaspora, which follows the fixture intensely.
headline: New Zealand Captain Santner Turns Down Big BBL Deal to Lead Against India
subheadline: The 34-year-old rejected a two-year Adelaide Strikers offer to keep his New Zealand central contract and white-ball captaincy ahead of the India home series.
